# Selling Partner API Documentation

> Welcome to Selling Partner API Documentation. Learn how to get started and build applications with Amazon's REST-based SP-API. Subscribe to updates via [RSS feed](http://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/changelog.rss).

Append .md to any documentation page URL to get its markdown version.

## Guides
- [Welcome to SP-API Documentation](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/welcome.md): Information about how to use the SP-API documentation site, and quick links for SP-API content.
- [What is the Selling Partner API?](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/what-is-the-selling-partner-api.md): This topic describes the REST-based Selling Partner API.
- [Selling Partner API Onboarding Overview](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/selling-partner-api-onboarding-overview.md): Determine which Selling Partner API onboarding path applies to you.
- [Onboarding as a Developer](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/onboarding-overview.md): Integrate your applications with Amazon's selling platform by using the Selling Partner API.
- [Step 1: Prepare for Registration](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/onboarding-step-1-prepare-for-registration.md): Gather the information and resources that you need to become an SP-API developer.
- [Step 2: Create a Solution Provider Portal Account](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/onboarding-step-2-create-an-spp-account.md): Create a Solution Provider Portal account to manage your SP-API applications.
- [Step 3: Create a Developer Profile](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/onboarding-step-3-create-a-developer-profile.md): Create a developer profile to manage your preferences and permissions.
- [Step 4: Register a Sandbox Application](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/onboarding-step-4-register-your-first-sandbox-application.md): Register a sandbox application in the Solution Provider Portal.
- [Step 5: Make Your First Call to the SP-API Sandbox](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/onboarding-step-5-make-your-first-call-to-the-sp-api-sandbox.md): Send test requests and receive responses in the SP-API sandbox environment.
- [Step 6: Set up the Authorization Workflow](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/onboarding-step-6-set-up-the-authorization-workflow.md): Configure how sellers authorize your application to call the SP-API on their behalf.
- [Step 7: Register Your Production Application](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/onboarding-step-7-register-your-first-production-application.md): Create your production application.
- [Step 8: Call the SP-API in Production](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/onboarding-step-8-call-the-sp-api-in-production.md): Connect to the SP-API by using manual HTTP requests or an SDK.
- [Step 9: Test Your Application](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/onboarding-step-9-test-your-application.md): Validate your application's functionality, security, and performance.
- [Step 10: List Your Application](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/onboarding-step-10-list-your-application.md): Create a listing for your application.
- [Onboarding as a Service Provider](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/service-provider-onboarding-overview.md): Essential steps to onboard as a service provider to help Amazon sellers manage their businesses.
- [Step 1: Learn the Service Provider Registration and Permissions Workflow](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/service-provider-onboarding-step-1.md): Learn the process that service providers and sellers take so that the service provider can act on behalf of the seller.
- [Step 2: Create a Solution Provider Portal Account for Your Company](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/service-provider-onboarding-step-2.md): Create the central account that your company will use to manage service provider operations.
- [Step 3: Verify Your Identity](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/service-provider-onboarding-step-3.md): Complete identity verification for yourself and your company in Solution Provider Portal.
- [Step 4: Complete the Service Profile for Your Company](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/service-provider-onboarding-step-4.md): Set up your business profile and describe the services that you offer.
- [Step 5: Apply for Seller Central Roles](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/service-provider-onboarding-step-5.md): Apply for the Seller Central roles that define the actions that you perform on behalf of sellers.
- [Step 6: Invite Employees to Your Account](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/service-provider-onboarding-step-6.md): Add employees to your company's Solution Provider Portal account.
- [Step 7: Connect With Sellers](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/service-provider-onboarding-step-7.md): Guide sellers through the process to authorize your company to access the seller's Seller Central account.
- [Step 8: List Your Service in the Service Provider Network](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/docs/service-provider-onboarding-step-8.md): Create a listing in the Service Provider Network so that Amazon sellers can discover your services.

- [createScheduledPackageBulk](https://developer-docs.amazon/sp-api/reference/createscheduledpackagebulk.md): This operation automatically schedules a time slot for all the `amazonOrderId`s given as input, generating the associated shipping labels, along with other compliance documents according to the marketplace (refer to the [marketplace document support table](doc:easyship-api-v2022-03-23-use-case-guide#marketplace-support-table)).  Developers calling this operation may optionally assign a `packageDetails` object, allowing them to input a preferred time slot for each order in ther request. In this case, Amazon will try to schedule the respective packages using their optional settings. On the other hand, *i.e.*, if the time slot is not provided, Amazon will then pick the earliest time slot possible.   Regarding the shipping label's file format, external developers are able to choose between PDF or ZPL, and Amazon will create the label accordingly.  This operation returns an array composed of the scheduled packages, and a short-lived URL pointing to a zip file containing the generated shipping labels and the other documents enabled for your marketplace. If at least an order couldn't be scheduled, then Amazon adds the `rejectedOrders` list into the response, which contains an entry for each order we couldn't process. Each entry is composed of an error message describing the reason of the failure, so that sellers can take action. The summaries returned depend on the presence or absence of the startDateTime, sellerSkus and sellerSku parameters:  - All inventory summaries with available details are returned when the startDateTime, sellerSkus and sellerSku parameters are omitted. - When startDateTime is provided, the operation returns inventory summaries that have had changes after the date and time specified. The sellerSkus and sellerSku parameters are ignored. Important: To avoid errors, use both startDateTime and nextToken to get the next page of inventory summaries that have changed after the date and time specified. - When the sellerSkus parameter is provided, the operation returns inventory summaries for only the specified sellerSkus. The sellerSku parameter is ignored. - When the sellerSku parameter is provided, the operation returns inventory summaries for only the specified sellerSku.  Note: The parameters associated with this operation may contain special characters that must be encoded to successfully call the API. To avoid errors with SKUs when encoding URLs, refer to [URL Encoding](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/url-encoding).
